source:
@@U04462@@
The ringing bell,
the scent of the lindens,
oppresses me with the feeling of church or the tomb.
The freedom of my will is laid waste in that sand.
How do I free my soul of this weight?
The bell tolls, while I go mad.

@@U04464@@
Yes, well, what can one expect?
Life is always soured by something or other.
That infernal jingle-jangle would distress anyone,
clouding the evening sky,
blighting everything between baptism and burial,
as if between a ding and a dong
life were no more than an idle dream.

@@U04466@@
That couple's perverse obstinacy
mars all my glorious profit. To my pain
I grow weary of being just.

@@U04468@@
Then why all these scruples?
Shouldn't you have relocated them long ago?

@@U04470@@
All right, then, get them out of my sight!
You know the pleasant little property
I'd set aside for them.

@@U04472@@
First we pick them up,
then set them down.
And before you know it,
they’re on their feet again.
Once they've seen the lovely little place,
they won't mind the violence it cost them.

@@U04473@@
(He whistles shrilly, Enter the THREE VIOLENT GIANTS.)
translation:
@@U04462@@
铃声响起，
椴树的香气，
教堂或坟墓的感觉压迫着我。
我的意志自由就在那片沙子里被毁掉了。
我怎样才能让我的灵魂摆脱这种沉重的负担？
钟声响起，我却发疯了。

@@U04464@@
是的，好吧，人们能期待什么？
生活总是会因为某些事情而变得糟糕。
那地狱般的叮当声会让任何人感到痛苦，
傍晚的天空乌云密布，
毁坏洗礼和埋葬之间的一切，
好像在叮和咚之间
生活只不过是一场无意义的梦。

@@U04466@@
那对夫妇的逆反心理
毁掉我所有光荣的利润。致我的痛苦
我厌倦了公正。

@@U04468@@
那为什么还要顾忌这些呢？
你不是应该早就把他们搬迁了吗？

@@U04470@@
好吧，那就让他们滚出我的视线吧！
你知道那令人愉快的小财产
我会为他们预留。

@@U04472@@
首先我们把它们捡起来，
然后把它们放下。
在你意识到之前，
他们又站起来了。
一旦他们看到了这个可爱的小地方，
他们不会介意这给他们带来的暴力。

@@U04473@@
（他尖声吹口哨，三个暴力巨人上。）
